acme_infra (customer): hi team — since yesterday our SSE streams to your API have been cutting out mid-response. client sees event data for a few seconds, then suddenly a 429 and the connection halts. partial output only. billing shows more tokens than we received.
Aisha (support): ugh, sorry to hear that. can you share the exact client request / curl you used, and whether you're using a long-lived key or ephemeral tokens? region?
acme_infra (customer): production long-lived API key (no rotation), region=us-west1. minimal curl: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer PROD_KEY_ABC" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/streams?model=gpt-rt"
```
Aisha (support): thanks — any rate limit headers returned before the 429? x-rate-limit, x-rl-reset, etc?
acme_infra (customer): none initially. we get 200 and SSE events (~3s), then raw HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests appended to the TCP stream and it closes. attached tcpdump to ticket.
Aisha (support): pinging runtime and sre — @Liam @Marina can you take a look?
Liam (runtime): possible quota enforcement mid-stream. normally we check quota at session start, but there are per-chunk safety metering calls. need x-request-id or trace id from your dump.
acme_infra (customer): request-id: req_9f2c8b1a. dump shows first SSE event block with text payload, then a comment line, then immediate 429.
Marina (sre): grabbing proxy logs for req_9f2c8b1a now  routed to pool-b. proxy shows initial 200 forwarded, then at ~3.1s the backend quota microservice returned 429 and proxy terminated the client connection. quota log: "quota-exceeded: used=1345, allowed=1200".
Olaf (billing): you said billed tokens=1345 but client saw ~800 tokens delivered?
acme_infra (customer): correct. client received about 800 visible tokens (stream cut mid-sentence). billing dashboard lists 1345 tokens for that request.
Liam (runtime): that pattern matches internal accounting vs delivered stream mismatch  the model may have generated tokens that were counted by internal meters but weren't flushed to the client before the connection closed. mid-stream 429 suggests a race in quota accounting across ledger shards.
Aisha (support): can we reproduce from our console using their key? the customer DM'd a scoped test key to me. attempting a replay.
deploy-bot: starting replay job for req_9f2c8b1a...
Aisha (support): repro successful from support machine: open SSE, stream events for ~3s then 429 and disconnect. raw TCP matches their dump.
Liam (runtime): i see the trace. the quota service issued a hard 429 from a different shard than the one consulted at stream initiation. we shard ledgers; initial check used shard-3, later metering delta applied to shard-7 which had a stale view and triggered enforce.
Marina (sre): root cause hypothesis: eventual-consistency between quota shards allows in-flight sessions to be overcounted on a different shard view; enforcement mid-stream causes abrupt HTTP 429 and connection close.
Olaf (billing): that could explain why billed = sum across shards, but client only saw pre-close output. also flag: our billing pipeline sums deltas from all shards and might double-count during handoffs; ive seen similar anomalies during shard rebalances.
acme_infra (customer): what's the workaround? we can't have streams terminate like this in production.
Liam (runtime): immediate workarounds: 1) temporary quota increase for affected key(s), 2) use Dedicated (reserved) deployment where metering is locally consistent, or 3) set a per-stream "max_tokens_reserved" param so runtime reserves headroom.
Aisha (support): i've requested a temporary quota bump for acme and CC'd their infra lead.
Marina (sre): repro steps we used for the internal sim: 1) open SSE session to a high-output model, 2) inject artificial delay in shard propagation between ledger nodes, 3) emit enough tokens to exceed the stale view on a different shard -> forced 429 mid-stream. attaching the simulation script to the ticket.
Liam (runtime): mitigation proposals: short-term patch to avoid hard 429 closes mid-stream; instead emit a structured SSE event and gracefully end so clients can reconcile. example: 
```
event: quota_exceeded
data: {"reason":"quota_exceeded","allowed":1200,"used":1345}
```
This prevents surprising HTTP-level errors and improves client observability.
Olaf (billing): and we should run a ledger reconciliation job to collapse shard deltas and produce canonical invoices; i'll take ownership of refunds review for customers with confirmed mid-stream 429 anomalies.
acme_infra (customer): could you also add rate-limit headers on the initial handshake so we can monitor usage before a failure? even x-rl-limit and x-rl-used would help.
Liam (runtime): agree. plan to put x-rl-limit and x-rl-used on the initial 200 response for SSE, and include the final used/limit values in the quota_exceeded SSE event.
Marina (sre): proposed immediate action items: 
1) hotfix: allow small inflight grace buffer + convert quota 429 mid-stream to structured SSE event (owner: liam, ETA: 48h)
2) add x-rate-limit headers on initial SSE response (owner: liam, ETA: 72h)
3) billing reconciliation plus refunds for impacted customers (owner: olaf, ETA: 5d)
4) infra RFC for stronger ledger consistency / bounded shard model (owner: infra-ml, ETA: 1 week)
Liam (runtime): also discovered a secondary cause in other incidents: certain gateways that reauth mid-connection (rotate Authorization) can create dual-session accounting and apparent double-billing. worth verifying if any customer proxies rewrite the auth header mid-stream.
acme_infra (customer): we do not rotate auth mid-connection. our nginx preserves the header and uses keepalives.
Aisha (support): logs confirm Authorization remained constant for req_9f2c8b1a. so likely cross-shard race as suspected.
Olaf (billing): i'll open a billing case and include the impacted request ids. pls attach the raw traces and tcpdumps for auditing.
acme_infra (customer): thanks. please CC our finance team as we'll need a statement for our books.
Liam (runtime): short-term client-facing guidance: if you need to avoid risk immediately, move to Dedicated or set max_tokens_reserved high per stream; we'll also document these mitigations.
Marina (sre): i'll spin up a dashboard to monitor shard propagation lag and alert if delta thresholds exceed safe bounds.
Aisha (support): marking as escalated to eng-runtime + billing. i'll update the customer with the mitigation timeline and the temporary quota bump.
deploy-bot: replay job finished; attached logs to ticket 3642.
Aisha (support): closing slack thread but keeping the support ticket open until refunds and hotfix are completed. will follow up in 24h with status. :thumbsup:
